<th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>

<tr><th class="th"><div>Jun. 30, 2026</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureAbstract', window );"><strong>Commitments and Contingencies Disclosure [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock', window );">CONTINGENCIES</a></td>
<td class="text"><p id="xdx_807_eus-gaap--CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock_zPUgVD6IlJGe" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 11: <span id="xdx_825_zGhZ148kVMK6">CONTINGENCIES</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In the normal course of business, the Company
may become involved in legal proceedings and claims. In accordance with ASC 450, Contingencies, the Company accrues a liability for such
matters when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated. When a range of
reasonably possible loss exists, the Company accrues the most probable amount within the range. If no amount within the range is a better
estimate than any other amount, the minimum amount in the range is accrued. Such accruals may include estimates of potential damages,
external legal fees, and other directly related costs expected to be incurred.&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Legal Proceedings</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Tazinique Echols v. Feel the World, Inc. (pre-litigation
ADA demand):</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On January 20, 2026, Feel the World, Inc. received
a pre-suit demand letter from Equal Access Law Group PLLC on behalf of&#160;Tazinique&#160;Echols, a visually impaired individual, alleging
that accessibility barriers on xeroshoes.com violated Title III of the ADA by preventing her from completing an online purchase; the letter
states an intent to seek injunctive relief, statutory damages where available, interest, and attorneys&#8217; fees if litigation is filed,
and offers to resolve the matter in exchange for remediation of the website and a $15,000.00 dollar payment and release. On June 1, 2026, the Company entered into a settlement agreement for $10,000 and the matter has been closed.</p>


<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"></p>


<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Anthony Devies v. Feel the World, Inc. d/b/a
Xero Shoes (threatened TCPA class action):&#160;&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On October 26, 2025, the class action firm Shamis
&amp; Gentile, P.A. sent a certified-mail demand letter to Feel the World, Inc. d/b/a Xero Shoes asserting that automated telemarketing
text messages were sent from short code 65099 to consumer Anthony Devies&#8217;cellular telephone without prior express consent and despite
his registration on the National Do Not Call Registry, and stating that, absent a response by November 16, 2025, counsel will pursue a
putative class action under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act seeking monetary and injunctive relief. As of March 17, 2026, Feel The
World, Inc.'s attorney filed a motion-to-dismiss and the Plaintiff&#8217;s opposition briefing is still to come.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><i>Leon Weingrad v. Feel the World, Inc.&#160;
</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">A putative class action was filed on January 1,
2026, alleging violations of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) for sending unsolicited marketing text messages to individuals
on the Do-Not-Call Registry and/or after opt-out requests.&#160; The Company has filed a motion to dismiss and/or strike the class allegations.
&#160;In response, the plaintiff filed an amended complaint, and the Company filed another motion to dismiss and/or strike the class allegations,
which remains pending. &#160;No settlement discussions have occurred, and the plaintiff has not provided a demand.&#160; It is too early
to determine the outcome, and the probability of loss cannot be assessed at this stage (neither probable nor remote).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of June 30, 2026, the Company has not
recorded any accruals for loss contingencies. While certain threatened litigation matters exist, these matters are in the early
stages, and management is unable to determine whether a loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to reasonably estimate the
amount or range of potential loss, if any. Accordingly, no provision has been recorded in the accompanying condensed consolidated
financial statements. The Company will continue to evaluate these matters as additional information becomes available.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i></i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Tariff Refunds</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Beginning in early 2025, additional tariffs
were imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (&#8220;IEEPA&#8221;) on products imported by the Company. In February
2026, the U.S. Supreme Court invalidated certain tariffs imposed under IEEPA, and in March 2026 the U.S. Court of International Trade
ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection to suspend collection of the invalidated tariffs and to establish a process to refund IEEPA
tariffs previously collected. During the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company received refunds of $<span id="xdx_904_ecustom--RefundReceived_c20260401__20260630_pp0p" title="Refund received"><span id="xdx_907_ecustom--RefundReceived_c20260101__20260630_pp0p" title="Refund received">49,374</span></span> of previously
paid IEEPA tariffs related to products sold in prior periods, which were recognized as a reduction of cost of revenue. Subsequent to June
30, 2026, the Company received additional refunds of $<span id="xdx_906_ecustom--RefundReceived_c20260701__20260928__us-gaap--SubsequentEventTypeAxis__us-gaap--SubsequentEventMember_pp0p" title="Refund received">1,823,401</span>. Consistent with the manner in which the related tariffs were originally
recorded, refunds of tariffs on products that have been sold are recognized as a reduction of cost of revenue, and refunds of tariffs
on products remaining in inventory are recorded as a reduction of the cost of that inventory and are recognized in cost of revenue as
the related products are sold.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></p>



<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"></p>




<span></span>
</td>
